answer: To enter, an agent must mill a cedar watermark into a locked collateral plank; the grain is unique and only revealable under a delayed key. At unpredictable times the protocol hoists a lantern roll-call: each live identity must answer with a one-shot gleam computed from its watermark and a just-settled work leaf. When many gleams arrive as one crest, settlement maps the ripple across shared keys, hosts, and watermark mills. Identities on that crest are treated as a coordinated swarm, collateral is burned by crest size, and their mill is barred from cutting new watermarks.
